labels.note: Table 4-1 in section 4 lists 'Young's modulus, steel' with symbol E, value 2 00E11 (interpreted as 2.00E11), and unit Pa. The claim correctly binds these to steel, uses Pa, cites the right section, and notes unknown basis since the table gives no further qualification. The quote captures the row content across columns.

The highlighted box reads exactly 'Reduced points: 100 < % of original weight < 110', so the range, unit, and quote are correct. The entity 'scoring' is vague (should specify Clothes Dryer Subcontest), the basis is clearly a rule/criterion rather than 'unknown', and the per-task/subcontest scope is omitted; the section field is also blank.

The source states hub height reaches 150 m, 'allowing for 30 m of ground (water surface) clearance with 120-m blades'—so 30 m is the blade-tip clearance above ground/water, not the ground/water depth. The claim binds 30 m to 'ground' as 'depth (water surface)' and omits 'clearance' from the quote, misreading the phrase.

Claim A correctly reads '2" x 4" FRAMING' in the deck footing detail (S-522, dc-cd). Claim B actually shows '2x4 CEDAR HANDRAILS' on exterior elevation A-202 (calg-cd), not general framing material; it misidentifies the component and truncates 'CEDAR'. The two items are different elements (deck framing vs handrails) from different design files, so they are not corresponding subjects.

The source shows Figure 7-1, a Bode plot with magnitude (dB) and phase (degrees) versus frequency for the generator-speed low-pass filter, consistent with the caption and text describing a recursive single-pole filter. The about correctly identifies the plot type and filter subject without citing numerical values; the role correctly frames it as illustrating the filter’s frequency response under the conditions discussed; keywords cover the core topics. No specific parameter values or design choices are given.

The drawing S-601 shows callout E6 for 'ROOF BEAM @ GRID 2,3,4,5 T.O. STEEL' with a beam diagram that includes the span dimension 21'-1 1/8". The value and entity match, but the quoted string stitches the callout text and the diagram dimension into one line, so it is not verbatim from a single location and does not fully support the claim as written.

Figure 2-6 shows the blade cross-section at 70% span titled 'Blade: IEA 15MW Offshore Reference Turbine; Section : 0.7', with a right-side color-bar legend that lists 'Carbon UD' among the material layers. The claim correctly reads this categorical label, quotes it verbatim, and attaches the right span/section condition. (The extractor context lists page 3, but the source image is page 12; this context error does not alter the claim's factual content.)

Figure 9 and its right-hand box show the cooking-subcontest scoring function: y-axis is 'Points per cooking task', x-axis is 'Weight of vaporized water (oz)', with a flat top at/above 80 oz indicating full (maximum) points, reduced points between 16 and 80 oz, and none below 16 oz. The claim correctly captures the chart, entity, attribute, unit, condition (≥80 oz), and section (9-2), but misstates the basis as 'unknown' when the source clearly presents a defined scoring rule, and incorrectly flags the reading as approximate when the 80 oz threshold is exact.

Figure 2-10(c) plots axial stiffness with y-axis in N scaled by 1e10. At r/R≈0.1 the curve is near ~2.5e10 N, falling sharply from the root; 4e10 N corresponds near r/R≈0, not at 0.1. The quote stitches axis labels rather than quoting a specific point.

Claim A correctly reads 25.0 m/s from the NREL 5-MW Region 3 sensitivity table; Claim B correctly reads the IEA 15-MW controller Region 3 range 10.59–25 m/s. They come from different turbine documents (5-MW vs 15-MW), so they describe different controllers, not a single corresponding subject.

Image 1 and Image 2 both show section 8-5, item d: 'If the dishwasher has a heated drying option, this option shall be disabled.' The entity, value, condition, quote, and section match the source exactly. However, the source is a regulatory requirement ('shall be disabled'), so labeling the basis as 'unknown' is incorrect; it should be a requirement.

The source crop (image 1) shows the drawing title 'SECTION - EAST MODULE' with the scale notation '3/8" = 1'-0"' directly beneath it, and the full page (image 2) places this in sheet A-301 Building Sections. The extracted value, quote, entity, and section match the source exactly with no misreading.

Figure 8 is a line graph with x-axis '% of original weight' and y-axis 'Points per clothes drying task', defining the Clothes Dryer Subcontest scoring. The about statement correctly names the figure, the two variables, and avoids specific values or thresholds. The role field is empty, but the about description itself is accurate and useful.

Image 1 shows the callout 'CEMENT FIBRE BOARD SIDING' at the top of the elevation drawing, and image 2 identifies the sheet as A-202 Exterior Elevations. The material and location are read correctly, though the source is a drawing annotation, not a table entry.

The image is sheet A-302 titled BUILDING SECTIONS, showing two cross-section drawings: C1 (Centre Module) with kitchen, bathroom, and mechanical room, and A1 (Living Room Section) with living rooms and kitchen, plus module and grade-level markers. The about text correctly names both sections, notes room designations and spatial layout across centre/west modules, and mentions floor-to-grade relationships without giving dimensions or design choices.

The crop shows the landscape footing detail with a 1'-0" wide footing and symmetric 4 1/4" dimensions from the 4x4 post faces to each footing edge; the left value is clearly labeled 4 1/4". The claim correctly identifies the post-related left offset, value, unit, quote, section, and diagram kind.

Figure 10 and the Contest 10 text show the scoring line reaching exactly 100 points at 0 kWh and remaining flat for net electrical energy ≥ 0 kWh, with full points defined for balance ≥ 0 kWh. So 100 points at 0 kWh is correct, but the point is a defined rule boundary, not an approximate chart reading, and the scoring applies at the conclusion of the specified balance period.
